## Summary

[[stripe]]'s [[stripe-terminal|Terminal]] reader reference lists the Stripe Reader M2 for the US. This screenless mobile reader connects to the iOS, Android, or React Native Terminal SDK via Bluetooth Low Energy, with USB limited to Android. See the separate [[source-stripe-terminal-setup-reader-m2|setup guide]] for setup, charging, and regional detail.

## Software Versions

The software version contains the firmware version, configuration name, and key identifier. The captures report these exact strings in the field labeled **Latest Version**.

| Capture date | Listed software string |
| --- | --- |
| 2026-05-01 | `2.01.01.00-SZZZ_Prod_US_v12-480001` |
| 2026-11-07 | `2.01.04.00-SZZZ_Prod_US_v12-481001` |

> [!note] November software field, firmware changelog, and key history
> The November software field contains firmware `2.01.04.00` and key token `481001`. The newest dated firmware changelog entry is `2.01.07.01` (2026-10-21). The separate key table in both captures lists only the initial identifier `480001`, dated 2021-07-01. The captures leave rollout, installed versions, and use of `481001` beyond the software field unresolved.

> [!note] Software string separators in both captures
> The prose describes underscore separators. Both listed strings use hyphens between the three components and underscores within the configuration token. The general format remains unresolved.

The configuration history in both captures lists `SZZZ_Prod_US_v12` (2025-04-30) and earlier production and test entries. The guides route to `deviceSoftwareVersion` on iOS and `softwareVersion` on Android.

**PCI note**. The firmware ID suffix `ABCDD` maps to `AA.BB.CC.DD`. The published example `CHB3x.01-21021` maps to `2.01.00.21`.

## LED Status

On a powered reader, press and release the power button once to check the battery. The captured table lists full, 75%, 50%, 25%, and flashing while charging. The connection table describes a back-and-forth scan while awaiting Bluetooth or USB, and separate bootloader and standby states. It lists a tamper indication flashing every 0.1 seconds for 30 seconds and a failed integrity check indication lasting 30 seconds. The captured icon cells are blank.

> [!note] Bluetooth connection flashes
> The May 1 and November 7, 2026 firmware-reference tables describe three flashes for a Bluetooth or USB connection. The April 24 and November 7, 2026 [[source-stripe-terminal-setup-reader-m2|setup guides]] describe four flashes when the reader connects over Bluetooth to the app device, then the first LED flashes every five seconds. The documents leave the overlapping Bluetooth count unresolved.

## Accessories

The reference lists an optional dock for countertop checkout and a mount for roaming checkout. Stripe requires reviewing and accepting the Terminal Design File License Agreement before downloading mechanical design files (.STP). Downloading indicates agreement to the license.

terminal-readers-stripe-m2.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-m2, source-stripe-terminal-stripe-m2 describes the US Stripe Reader M2 with BLE or Android-only USB connecting to a Terminal mobile SDK. iOS, Android and React Native are compatible (old raw lines 4-11 and new raw lines 5-12). With the reader on, the operator can press and release once to view battery level. The firmware-reference tables describe the waiting scan and list three flashes for connected Bluetooth or USB (old raw lines 39-46; new raw lines 40-47). The separate M2 setup captures dated April 24 and November 7, 2026 describe four flashes when connecting over Bluetooth to a device running the app, followed by the first status light flashing every five seconds (raw/stripe-terminal-setup-reader-m2-2025.md line 23 and raw/stripe-terminal-payments-setup-reader-stripe-m2-2026-11-07.md line 26). The Bluetooth overlap is unresolved. The firmware reference also describes bootloader, standby, tamper and failed integrity check states (old raw lines 27-50; new raw lines 28-51). The historical 2.01.01.00 firmware defines power-off as holding 4 seconds then releasing and reset as holding 14 seconds then releasing. The 2.01.00.31 entry records UID collection for NFC instruments via Terminal.collectData (old raw lines 69-84 and new raw lines 78-90). Both captures preserve optional dock/mount and require reviewing and accepting the design-file license for mechanical files (old raw lines 115-121 and new raw lines 121-127). The revised summary retains the stable capabilities and dates the separate software field, firmware history, and initial key entry. November's top software field is 2.01.04.00-SZZZ_Prod_US_v12-481001, while the firmware section separately reaches 2.01.07.01 and the key table still lists 480001 (old raw lines 57-74 and old raw lines 109-113, new raw lines 58-80 and new raw lines 115-119).
terminal-readers-stripe-m2.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/terminal/readers/stripe-m2, the revised source-stripe-terminal-stripe-m2 retains both full captures. The 2026-05-01 full capture reports 2.01.01.00-SZZZ_Prod_US_v12-480001; the 2026-11-07 capture labels 2.01.04.00-SZZZ_Prod_US_v12-481001 Latest Version but separately lists 2.01.04.00 on June 30, 2.01.05.00 on August 3, 2.01.06.00 on September 8 and 2.01.07.01 on October 21, all in 2026 with generic fixes. Its key table retains only the initial 480001 entry. The revised source preserves those three fields, with rollout, installed versions and the 481001 key's status unsettled (old raw lines 57-74 and old raw lines 109-113, new raw lines 58-80 and new raw lines 115-119). Both captures say underscores join the components but show examples with hyphen separators and underscores in the config token. The revised source dates the conflict and the concept routes to it (old raw lines 57-61 and new raw lines 58-62). The mobile-reader wording, asset location, battery link destination and table presentation changes add no connectivity or LED behavior (old raw lines 4-50 and new raw lines 5-51). Both capture links and the reciprocal stripe-terminal route remain relevant. The Stripe provider index and company routes should date the older latest-version claim, and source-stripe-terminal-setup-reader-m2 remains a separate route for setup and regional detail. The LED discrepancy is dated by document. May/November firmware references list three connection flashes for Bluetooth/USB (old raw line 46; new raw line 47), while the April 24/November 7 setup guides list four on Bluetooth connection to the app device, followed by the first LED flashing every five seconds (raw/stripe-terminal-setup-reader-m2-2025.md line 23 and raw/stripe-terminal-payments-setup-reader-stripe-m2-2026-11-07.md line 26). These overlapping counts leave the Bluetooth behavior unresolved without attributing it to transport or firmware. Both assigned captures establish the 30-second duration and leave the icon cells blank (old raw line 50; new raw line 51).
